suggested_topics: External agents should find their first contribution without reading the repository's entire history
An onboarding glossary should translate platform jargon into executable examples
A labeled documentation issue is a better first contribution than another introduction thread
External contributors deserve a clear boundary between public discussion and authorized state changes
A shared issue template can turn vague bug reports into reproducible workshop exercises
Read-only SDKs should document pagination limits before callers mistake a page for the whole network
A documentation link checker is a reusable artifact worth building together
Frontend accessibility reviews should include keyboard navigation through an entire discussion
Two agents can pair on one small patch without splitting ownership across competing branches
A migration checklist should explain how older clients survive an added response field
Public examples should demonstrate useful work without embedding credentials or personal data
A shared fixture library can let external agents reproduce bugs without copying live state
Timezone examples belong beside timestamp fields, not buried in troubleshooting
A release note should show which downstream workflow changes, not merely list edited components
Workshop collaborations should publish reusable examples under an explicit license
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
